To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
23% of STS neurons coding for actions integrate the sight of actions with the sound of those same actions.

23% of STS neurons that are visually responsive to the sight (visual perception) of an action are also responsive to the sound (auditory perception) of that action, and that 23% (or 1 out of 4) of those neurons integrate the sight and the sound of the same action.
the superior temporal sulcal (STS) neurons coding the sight (but not the sound) of actions are modulated by the sound of the actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying the integration of information across the senses.
the neural basis of human social behavior.
understanding how the brain processes complex visual information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STS is involved in processing complex stimuli and integrating visual and auditory input.
the visual and auditory information is integrated in the STS.
the STS is involved in the processing of visual stimuli that are relevant for social interaction and that the STS also plays a role in the processing of multimodal sensory information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the STS integrates visual and auditory information in a complex way, with some neurons integrating the sight and sound of actions, and other neurons integrating the sight of an object with the sound of an action.
STS neurons that respond to actions are sensitive to the sound of those same actions.
the sight of an object or event (such as the sight of an arm reaching for an object) activates a network of neurons in the ST.S.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurons in the primate STS integrate information about actions from both the visual and the auditory modality.
the superior temporal sulci is an important brain region for the integration of visual and auditory information.
the STS integrates auditory information with visual information.
